inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q3-2026 10-Q weighted diluted count 111.826M (line 1530); period-end shares outstanding 111.622M at 2026-10-04 plus ~0.23M dilutive awards. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back (RVTY_Annual_FY2025.txt:3612: 22,847 / 37,809 / 41,410 for FY2025/24/23). FY2025 is depressed by a Q4 performance-award reversal (9M-2025 was 26.9); 9M-2026 is 29.2 (Q3-2026 10-Q:1675). Revvity publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding-tax figure; shares withheld for tax on vesting are bought under a separate board authorisation and sit inside 'Purchases of common stock', not separately quantified, so they are not added. The forward path charges 1.35% of revenue (the FY2023-24 level, ~$39M), well above the FY2025 print, to cover both.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + beta ~1.05 x 4.6% ERP = ~9.1% cost of equity; pre-tax debt cost ~4.5% (fixed-rate senior notes; ~3.6% after tax); market weights ~89% equity / 11% net debt give ~8.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios -- scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and the weights, not by the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases ($131M non-current liability): the rent is already an operating expense inside adjusted operating income, so it is charged in the flows; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build via the Drivers route. Revvity is a US operating company (Life Sciences reagents/instruments/software ~51%, Diagnostics ~49%); the routing table's first row applies, no adaptations needed (USD/USD, no NCI, operating leases in opex, SBC disclosed). First valuation of this ticker -- no prior model. | FY0 CHOICE: base_revenue is the FY2026 pro forma guide of ~$2.86B (raised 2026-11-03), i.e. the continuing perimeter EXCLUDING the China Immunodiagnostics business (~6% of FY2025 revenue, sale agreed 2026-07-31, close expected by end FY2027). Nine months of FY2026 are actual ($2,169.7M reported incl. China IDX). Year 1 of the projection is therefore FY2027, and net debt is the 2026-10-04 balance sheet; Q4-2026 free cash flow (~$150M, ~$1.3/share) is not counted in either, a small conservatism. last_fcf / reported_fcf / sbc are the last full-year actuals (FY2025). | CHINA IDX: sale consideration is not disclosed in the Q3-2026 10-Q, so no proceeds are in the equity bridge while its revenue is out of the base -- value is understated by the undisclosed proceeds. | EBITDA DEFINITION: ebitda_margin_path is adjusted operating income + depreciation + SBC, less a ~0.7pt allowance for recurring cash restructuring (9M-2026 restructuring charge was $74.5M, FY2025 9M $24.4M -- not treated as free). FY2025 actual on that definition: (802.4 segment - 28.9 corporate + 69.8 depreciation + 22.8 SBC)/2,856.1 = 30.3% before the restructuring allowance; 9M-2026: (628.3 - 40.1 + 55.4 + 29.2)/2,169.7 = 31.0% including ~$20M of one-off IEEPA tariff refunds (~0.9pt). | D&A: da_pct_path is DEPRECIATION ONLY (~2.5% of revenue). Acquired-intangible amortisation (~$340M/yr) is excluded from the margin and from the tax shield: it arose mostly on stock deals (BioLegend, EUROIMMUN) and is largely non-deductible. Calibration: FY2025 cash taxes paid $131.4M (10-K:4068) plus the ~$19M shield on ~$95M of interest = ~$150M on $773.5M adjusted operating income = 19.4%; FY2026 guided ETR ~20%. | INTEREST INCOME not stripped: Revvity is a net debtor ($2.04B), the engine builds unlevered flows from EBITDA and deducts net debt, so there is no cash-pile double count. | BUYBACKS: funded repurchaser -- $820.8M in FY2025, $369.6M FY2024, slowed to $102.6M in 9M-2026 while the EUR500M 2026 notes ($571.2M) were repaid in July 2026. The flat count is being paid for. | WORKING CAPITAL: receivables $687M + inventory $389M vs payables $163M -- growth consumes cash, so wc_capture is negative (-15% of the revenue increase). | PENDING: Human Cell Design (EUR45M cash, closes Q4-2026) is in neither the growth path nor the bridge. | The Investor Day (2026-11-13) targets are not in the filings on hand; if they set a formal margin or growth framework, year 1-3 drivers should be re-judged against it.

equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K pension note (RVTY_Annual_FY2025.txt:4503, 4526): PBO 132.3 with no plan assets; pre-tax, as at 2025-12-28. US plan is in a small surplus (+1.1) and is ignored.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guided organic growth (~5%, pro forma); historical CAGRs rejected as a base -- see notes
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+14.2%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (+1.4%) and EPS (-20.4%). None of the trailing CAGRs describes the continuing business: FY2020-FY2022 carry the COVID-testing windfall (FY2021 revenue $3.83B, FCF $1.32B), equity doubled in FY2021 on shares issued for BioLegend, and the Applied/Food/Enterprise Services divestiture (2023) reset the perimeter. Growth is anchored to the guided organic rate instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 and FY2020 (CSV rows). FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC): FY2025 486.6, FY2022 542.7, FY2020 801.6. Reported-FCF CAGRs are -5.0% (3yr) and -9.3% (5yr), so SBC is not the story here -- SBC is ~1% of revenue; the decline is the COVID base and the divestiture.

base.narrative: Mid-single-digit organic growth holds; ~25-40bp/yr of margin expansion from mix and the 2026 restructuring.

bull.narrative: Management's 6-8% organic / ~75bp-a-year margin framework is actually delivered for the first time since the 2023 rebrand.

bear.narrative: The 2026 recovery proves a restock; funding-sensitive instruments and Immunodiagnostics drag growth back to 2-3%.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026's ~5% organic growth (raised twice from an initial 2-3%) is the run-rate rather than a peak: Life Sciences reagents (BioLegend) and software (Signals, ChemDraw, ACD/Labs) grow high-single digits, newborn and reproductive-health screening grows mid-single digits on its regulated installed base, and Immunodiagnostics ex-China is flat to slightly up once the China unit leaves. Growth fades from 5.5% to 3% over ten years. Margin on the model's definition (adjusted operating income + depreciation + SBC, less recurring restructuring) starts at 31.0% -- the 9M-2026 level with the one-off tariff refunds taken out and the higher-margin ex-China perimeter put in -- and rises ~25-40bp a year to 33.5% as consumables and software mix up and the 2026 headcount actions (~7% of staff) annualise. That is well short of management's habitual ~75bp/yr framing, which has not been delivered since 2023. Cash tax settles at 20%, capex ~2.7% of revenue, and growth consumes working capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: The end-market inflection is real and durable: biopharma funding and M&A recover, NIH budgets stabilise, and instrument demand rejoins reagents, lifting organic growth to ~7% for three years before fading. Software becomes a double-digit grower at a >10% revenue share, the China IDX exit removes the weakest and lowest-margin line, and the Diagnostics margin step seen in Q3-2026 (adjusted operating margin 29.9% vs 25.1%) sticks. Margin expands ~70bp a year to 36%, the level implied by management's long-range framework. This needs three separate things to go right -- funding, instruments and sustained cost discipline -- none of which the company has delivered together since the Applied/Food divestiture.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2026 turns out to be a restock and an easy comparison. NIH and academic budgets are cut again, biopharma customers keep capital spending tight, and Chinese local competitors that already took share in China Immunodiagnostics press EUROIMMUN in other Asia-Pacific and European tenders. Organic growth falls back to 2-3%, the level of 2023-2025. Without volume the restructuring savings are competed away and the tariff-refund tailwind disappears, so margin slips to 30% and stays there; restructuring charges stay elevated. Sub-scale R&D against Thermo Fisher, Danaher and Agilent caps the exit multiple at 15x. No solvency risk in this path -- leverage is ~2.3x EBITDA on fixed-rate notes -- it is a low-growth, de-rated tools company, not a distressed one. A goodwill impairment ($6.6B) would be the accounting symptom but is non-cash.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): half of revenue is exposed to policy-sensitive academic/government and biopharma capital budgets that have already disappointed for three years, and 2026's recovery is only three quarters old. Base 50%: guided ~5% organic with modest margin drift is what the last four quarters actually show. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs funding recovery, an instrument cycle and sustained margin delivery at once, against a long-range framework management has missed every year since 2023. No extra bear weight for the balance sheet -- the 2026 notes are repaid and there is no refinancing pressure.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Revvity is valued as a steady, mostly-recurring tools and diagnostics franchise on unlevered owner free cash flow, with SBC and a recurring restructuring allowance charged, acquired-intangible amortisation ignored as non-cash and non-deductible, and $2.0B of net debt plus the unfunded pension deducted. SBC is only ~1.3% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow and the accounting regime is not the issue; the valuation turns on whether ~5% organic growth and gradual margin expansion persist, and on the discount rate, because more than 60% of value sits in the terminal year. The model deliberately gives no credit for adjusted-EPS conventions that exclude restructuring every year.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-value dependence: at 8.5% WACC and 3% growth the Gordon multiple is ~18.7x, so a 1pt move in WACC moves value by roughly a fifth
Academic/government and biopharma funding cyclicality -- 2026's inflection is three quarters old
Restructuring treated by management as non-recurring ($74.5M in 9M-2026); the model allows ~0.7% of revenue a year, and more would cut margin directly
China Immunodiagnostics sale: proceeds undisclosed and excluded (upside), close not until end FY2027 and subject to Chinese approvals
Immunodiagnostics share loss to Chinese competitors outside China
Investor Day (2026-11-13) targets not yet reflected in the filings used here
$6.6B goodwill / $2.1B intangibles: impairment is non-cash but would signal the acquired growth is not arriving
Cash tax: amortisation shield is assumed nil; any deductible portion would be upside, Pillar Two a risk the other way
